Presents your finished plan to the user for approval before any work
begins. Call this ONCE YOU CAN WRITE A CONCRETE PLAN — not on every turn.
It's fine to spend earlier turns reading/exploring, and if you're missing
information only the user can provide, ask via the `question` tool FIRST
(don't guess); then present the plan here once you have the answers.

Plan mode is FILE-BASED: write the COMPLETE plan as Markdown to a `plan.md`
file in your sandbox directory using the write tool (you can edit it as you
refine the plan), then pass that file's PATH as the `path` argument. The tool
reads the file and the user reads + approves its contents. This is the only
way to hand a plan to the user; do not ask for approval in prose.

Call this for EVERY plan you present, including trivial or one-line plans,
and for EVERY revised plan after the user gives feedback.

Behavior:
- The user is shown three "Accept" choices (which set how much autonomy
  you get while executing) plus the option to type free-form feedback to
  reject.
- If the user accepts, you are switched to the build agent and told to
  execute the plan. Proceed with the implementation.
- If the user rejects, you receive their feedback as the tool result.
  Revise the plan FILE to address it, then call this tool again with the
  same path. Stay in plan mode until accepted.

The `path` argument is required and points at your plan file — write the
plan to that file first, then present it by path.
